properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata comprise Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock with volcanic basalt intrusions of the Lothian formation. Facade masonry consists of pale buff-to-grey Craigleith quartz-arenite sandstone ashlar over Hailes sandstone rubble footings. Mortar is historic hot-mixed hydraulic lime with graded quartz aggregate.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Bordering parkland features mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late September phenology: full canopy volumes exhibiting early autumn senescence, chlorotic margin yellowing, and minor crown defoliation.

properties.architectural_summary: Georgian Neo-Classical civic and residential terrace composition (Robert Adam design executed by Robert Reid, early 19th century). Dominated by West Register House (former St George's Church) featuring a colossal Ionic portico, multi-tiered square clock base, circular columnar drum, and high copper dome. Adjoining unified terraces comprise three-storey plus attic and sunken basement profiles, characterized by ground-level channelled ashlar rustication, smooth dressed upper ashlar, regular 6-over-6 timber sash fenestration, projecting string courses, mutule cornices, and parapet balustrades.
